description:
TIRED OF MEETING THE PRODUCT AT THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS STAGE?

Most product lawyers see the flow once it's built and the launch date is set. Here, you're on the whiteboard at ideation, so compliant by design is the plan, not the clean-up.

And the stakes are real. Taptap Send moves billions of dollars every month across 100 countries, and is now building wallets, cards and broader financial products for diaspora communities.

THE JOB

You'll advise on new licensing and products from first idea to go-live, and own regulator engagement across our markets.

- Shape products before they're built: review designs, UX, flows and terms against regulatory and customer-outcome rules, Consumer Duty included, while change is still cheap.

- Turn regulation into decisions: what's mandatory, what's prudent, and the alternative route that still gets it launched.

- Own the regulator relationship: across our markets, including new ones, and flag what regulatory change means for the roadmap early.

- Take products to new countries: localise what already works, with country leads and local counsel.

- Build the playbooks: templates that let Legal scale without adding friction.

WHY YOU'LL WANT IT

Spend your time on the hard questions. You're asked to shape our roadmap and launches, and understand how to fit them to the relevant regimes

Be a peer, with room to run. You'll join a flat team of regulatory and commercial lawyers, with real autonomy and a manager who trusts you.

Make launches faster, not slower. Legal in the room from day one is how products here ship sooner. That's the whole point of your seat.

Make sending money home cheaper. Remittances pay for school fees, rent and medical bills, and are worth more than all foreign aid combined. Cheaper, reliable transfers put more of that money in families' hands.

IS THIS YOU?

You're a qualified lawyer (UK or equivalent) with 4+ years' PQE in payments, e-money or financial services regulation, at a firm, a regulator or a fintech.

You've advised payments or e-money firms under the FCA or an equivalent regime, dealt with the regulator directly, and helped product teams take live launches over the line.

You give the answer first and the reasoning second. Ambiguity across several jurisdictions doesn't stop you making the call.

title: Director, Incident Response
description:
Job Title: Director, Incident Response
Job Location: Parsippany, New Jersey, United States of America
Job Location Type: Remote
Job Contract Type: Full-time
Job Seniority Level:
The Director, Incident Response leads enterprise‑scale execution of cybersecurity incident response activities, ensuring effective detection, containment, investigation, and recovery from security incidents. This role operationalizes incident response strategy, oversees readiness and execution across multiple domains, and acts as a senior escalation point for significant incidents. The Director partners closely with technology, legal, compliance, and business leaders to ensure response actions align with regulatory requirements and organizational risk tolerance, safeguarding the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information assets. This role also oversees the organization's digital forensics capability, ensuring forensic investigations are conducted with evidentiary rigor to support incident resolution, legal proceedings, and regulatory obligations.

Responsibilities :

• Leads execution of enterprise incident response operations, including detection, investigation, containment, eradication, and recovery.

• Oversees incident response readiness, including play books, escalation procedures, testing, and simulation exercises.

• Acts as a senior escalation point and incident commander for high‑severity cybersecurity incidents.

• Coordinates cross‑functional response activities with security operations, IT, legal, privacy, compliance, and communications teams.

• Ensures incident handling meets regulatory, legal, and contractual notification requirements.

• Reviews post‑incident analysis, root‑cause investigations, and remediation plans to reduce recurrence.

• Defines and monitors incident response metrics and effectiveness indicators for leadership reporting.

• Leads and develops incident response managers and senior technical specialists.

• Serves as the senior incident commander for high‑severity cybersecurity incidents, breaches, and crises.

• Directs digital forensics investigations during significant incidents, ensuring forensic processes align with legal hold requirements and evidentiary standards.

• Collaborates with legal and compliance teams to ensure forensic findings are properly documented and defensible for regulatory or litigation purposes.

Experience:

• 10+ years of progressive cybersecurity experience.

• 7+ years of significant hands-on experience in incident response, DFIR, SOC operations, threat hunting, security investigations, or related cybersecurity disciplines.

• 3+ years of experience leading cybersecurity professionals, including managers and/or senior technical personnel.

• Demonstrated experience leading major or enterprise-scale cybersecurity incidents involving multiple technology and business teams.

• Experience operating in a large, geographically distributed enterprise environment.

• Demonstrated experience communicating cybersecurity incidents and risk to senior executives.

Strong Knowledge of:

• Cybersecurity incident response and incident command

• Digital forensics and evidence preservation

• Endpoint detection and response (EDR/XDR)

• SIEM and security analytics

• SOAR and security automation

• Microsoft Windows and Active Directory

• Entra ID / cloud identity

• Microsoft 365 security

• AWS and/or Azure incident investigation

• Network security and network forensics

• Malware and ransomware investigations

• Email compromise and phishing investigations

• Identity and credential compromise

• Threat intelligence and threat hunting

• MITRE ATT&CK

• NIST Cybersecurity Framework and NIST SP 800-61

• Root-cause analysis and post-incident review
